title: DRDO Signs First High-Value TDF Pact with Startup Zero mK India for 20 mK Dilution Refrigerator - Quantum Computing Report
gist: India's DRDO signed the first high-value project under its expanded ₹500-crore (~$52.2M) Technology Development Fund with startup Zero mK India to build an indigenous 20 mK dilution refrigerator, mentored by DRDO's SSPL Delhi, to cut dependence on Western cryogenic vendors for quantum computing and defense. The short news item does not disclose the contract's own value or timeline, and it wrongly calls 20 mK a 'sub-absolute-zero' environment.

insights.claim: India's Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) signed its first high-value deep-tech project under the Technology Development Fund (TDF) scheme with domestic startup Zero mK India to engineer and build a 20 millikelvin dilution refrigerator.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Indian defense funding is going straight to startups building quantum enabling hardware. That points to more state-backed contracts for domestic cryogenics and quantum supply-chain companies.
insights.locator: India’s Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)

insights.claim: The DRDO-Zero mK India contract is the first high-value project sanctioned under the expanded ₹500-crore (about $52.2 million) TDF deep-tech corpus approved by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The size of the Zero mK contract itself is not disclosed.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Most of the ~$52M corpus is still unallocated. Watch for the next TDF deep-tech awards, which may go to quantum, sensing or other strategic hardware startups.
insights.quote: the first high-value project sanctioned under the expanded ₹500-crore (~$52.2 million USD) TDF corpus
insights.locator: The agreement represents the first high-value

insights.claim: The director and scientific team at DRDO's Solid State Physics Laboratory (SSPL) in Delhi monitor, mentor and technically evaluate the Zero mK India dilution refrigerator project. The state is actively guiding the work, not only funding it.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Close technical oversight by a DRDO lab lowers execution risk. It also makes a later defense procurement channel for Zero mK India more likely.
insights.locator: The project is monitored, mentored, and technically evaluated

insights.claim: Dilution refrigerators that reach about 20 mK are needed to preserve phase coherence in solid-state quantum processors, including superconducting circuits, silicon spin qubits and quantum sensing arrays. This makes them essential enabling hardware for several qubit types.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cryogenic suppliers are a 'picks and shovels' play across several qubit types. Demand for their hardware grows whichever solid-state approach wins.
insights.locator: Dilution refrigerators provide the ultra-low temperature

insights.claim: The Zero mK India system targets 20 mK (0.02 K) operation using sub-kelvin 3He/4He dilution circulation, aimed at scalable quantum processor (QPU) testing and packaging.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The fridge is positioned as QPU test and packaging infrastructure. It is a specification target, not a demonstrated result, so watch for performance milestones before crediting the capability.
insights.locator: DRDO TDF Deep-Tech Cryogenic Project Overview

themes.theme: Sovereign supply chain and import substitution

insights.claim: India is funding domestic dilution refrigerator development to cut its dependence on Western cryogenic vendors and reduce sovereign import risk for specialized sub-kelvin equipment.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Incumbent Western dilution refrigerator makers face long-term share loss in India as governments treat quantum hardware as strategic and localize supply. The same move could spread to other nations pursuing quantum independence.
insights.quote: Reduces import dependency on Western cryo vendor systems
insights.locator: DRDO TDF Deep-Tech Cryogenic Project Overview

insights.claim: The DRDO-Zero mK India cryogenics project is aligned with India's National Quantum Mission and is meant to serve domestic research labs, defense communication programs and commercial quantum hardware developers building sovereign quantum computing infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The planned customers span defense and civilian users, so domestic demand has several sources. That can support a local quantum hardware supplier ecosystem in India.
insights.locator: Aligning with India’s National Quantum Mission (NQM)
